title: Slow-Roast Lamb Shoulder
subtitle: Long-cooked lamb shoulder that falls apart at a touch
excerpt: Lamb shoulder slow-roasted for four to five hours at low heat until the meat collapses from the bone and can be served by pulling it apart with two forks. No carving needed; the most forgiving and rewarding way to cook lamb.

recipe.sourceNotes: Slow-roasted lamb shoulder is associated with Greek, Middle Eastern, and Italian cooking (where it appears as agnello al forno) but is also traditional in British cooking for Sunday lunch. The shoulder is a working muscle with significant connective tissue and fat, which makes it ideal for long, slow cooking: at around 150°C over four to five hours, the collagen in the connective tissue converts to gelatin, the fat renders out and bastes the meat, and the muscle fibres become so tender they pull apart without effort. The technique requires no technical skill; the only requirement is time. Stuffing the shoulder with garlic, rosemary, and anchovy before cooking adds depth from the inside out.

content.text: Use a shoulder on the bone; boneless shoulders are faster but the bone adds flavour and the structure helps the meat hold its shape during cooking. Cover the roasting tin tightly with two layers of foil so no steam escapes. The lamb should be so tender it pulls apart without cutting; if it doesn't, it needs another 30 minutes.

items.preparation: halved lengthways; to stud the lamb

content.text: Heat the oven to 160°C / fan 140°C / gas 3. Use a small sharp knife to make 20 to 30 cuts all over the lamb, each about 2 cm deep. Into each cut push a piece of garlic and a piece of anchovy. Rub the outside with olive oil, then season generously with salt and pepper.

Put the onion halves in a roasting tin and pour in the wine and stock. Set the lamb on top. Cover the tin tightly with a double layer of foil. Roast for 4 to 5 hours until the meat pulls away from the bone effortlessly.

Remove the foil and increase the heat to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Roast uncovered for a further 20 minutes to crisp the outside. Rest for 20 minutes. Serve by pulling the meat apart with two forks, pouring the defatted pan juices over as a sauce.
